subject: SLA-driven tradeoffs + pilot budgeting — streaming vs batching options
summary: Post-demo qualification focusing on token volumes, target $/1M tokens, and latency vs cost tradeoffs. Agreement to run a 4-week pilot with two config arms (streaming low-latency vs batched cost-optimized) and deliver an SLO-driven quote.
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@quickserve.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pilot sizing + SLA tradeoffs (streaming vs batch)

Alex — great conversation today, thanks for walking through the QuickServe search use cases. Per our call I wanted to put the numbers and options in writing so we can lock scope for a pilot. High-level notes and asks below.

1) Confirmed volumes and shapes (please reply with any corrections):
- Average tokens per request: ~1.6k (search + small context)
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: 50M–75M
- Peak concurrency: ~180 simultaneous requests (30–60s bursts)
- Latency objective for 95th percentile: 200–300 ms (hard SLO for core UX)

2) Target unit economics (you mentioned finance is aiming for):
- Target $/1M tokens: $200 (goal) — design pilot to show delta vs $200 at scale
- Monthly budget band for pilot scale (4 weeks): $5k–$15k (flexible)

3) Tradeoffs we recommend testing in pilot (two arms):
- Arm A "Low-latency streaming": prioritize P95 latency <= 220 ms by using a dedicated low-latency tier, model variant tuned for shorter latency, aggressive prefix caching, and streaming tokens to the client. Expected delta vs baseline: ~+25–40% cost per 1M tokens but meets UX SLO.
- Arm B "Cost-optimized batching": prioritize unit cost by using continuous batching + larger micro-batch windows and slightly higher P95 (~350–450 ms). Expected cost reduction: ~25–35% vs the streaming arm.

4) Measurement and acceptance:
- We'll instrument P95, p50, cost per 1M tokens, and quality regressions (prompt eval set).
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: either meet latency SLO with cost within 20% of target $/1M, or hit target $/1M while keeping quality within 2% of baseline.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm volumes and budget band by EOD Wed (2 business days).
- We provision two parallel pilot configs (streams vs batch) and share a one-page pilot scope + PO template.
- Kickoff call to run instrumentation and anti-regression checks, target start: Mar 7.

Attachments: [Attachment: pilot-scope.pdf (12 KB, PDF)] [Attachment: po-template.docx (18 KB, DOCX)]

Thanks — I’ve looped Marissa to help with the cost modeling. If procurement is involved please cc Julie so we can share the PO template.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
[kim@redwood.ai]

From: Alex Moreno <alex@quickserve.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@quickserve.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pilot sizing + SLA tradeoffs (streaming vs batch)

Thanks Kimberly — this is super helpful and lines up with what we discussed internally. Quick confirmations and one clarification: 

- Avg tokens/request: 1.6k is correct (range 800–2.5k depending on user session)
- Monthly tokens: leaning toward the 60M mark to be conservative for forecast
- Peaks: 180 concurrent is accurate during our morning ingest window
- Latency target: 250ms P95 is the team goal — 200ms would be best but 250ms is acceptable

On the budget: procurement would like to see a capped pilot spend — we can sign a PO up to $12k for the 4-week pilot. Julie is on copy, she will confirm if that works from procurement after we see the pilot scope.

One ask: can you include a short table in the scope showing estimated cost per 1M tokens for both arms (stream vs batch) using our 60M/month baseline? That will make it easier for procurement to evaluate.

Happy to kickoff Mar 7 if you can get the scope over this week.

—Alex
Head of Product, QuickServe.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@quickserve.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pilot sizing + SLA tradeoffs (streaming vs batch)

Alex — perfect, appreciate the quick confirmation. Julie — welcome, and thanks in advance for reviewing the pilot PO cap. Attached is an updated one-pager with the quick cost table and a short mutual action plan. Copying the table here for convenience (estimates use your 60M tokens/month baseline):

Estimated unit math (60M tokens/mo baseline):
- Streaming (low-latency tier): ~ $260 / 1M tokens -> monthly = $15,600 (delta vs target $200 = +30%)
- Batched (cost-optimized): ~ $175 / 1M tokens -> monthly = $10,500 (delta vs target $200 = -12.5%)

Notes: these estimates include expected model variant efficiency, continuous KV caching for prefixes, and an allowance for 8% traffic amplification during peak windows. We’ll provide exact per-route quotes for the pilot once we instrument a 48-hour profiling run against a small sample of your traffic.

Mutual action plan (short):
- You: sign PO cap ($12k) or confirm internal approval for $15,600 pilot if you prefer the low-latency arm only — due by Thu EOD.
- Redwood: provision two pilot configs, run 48-hour profiler, deliver per-route cost + latency breakdown, and share SLO dashboard.
- Joint: kickoff Mar 7, run 4-week pilot, mid-pilot check on week 2 to adjust batch windows or fallback routing.

I attached pilot-scope.pdf with the table and a PO template that Julie can use. If the PO cap is $12k we’ll scope the pilot to focus the first two weeks on the batched arm and the latter two weeks shifting traffic to streaming for a short validation window so you can see the tradeoffs without exceeding the cap.

Ben — would you be able to run the 48-hour profiling and a quick cost simulation so we can hand Julie the final numbers?

Thanks — Kim

Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pilot sizing + SLA tradeoffs (streaming vs batch)

Looping in from Engineering side — I’ll own the profiling and cost sim. Plan:
- Start a 48-hour profiler against a 1% traffic mirror on Mar 3 (today) to capture latency distribution, token counts, and KV cache hit rates.
- Deliverables by Fri EOD: per-route cost table for both arms at 60M tokens/mo baseline, expected P95 for streaming vs batching, and a short recommendation with contingencies.

Preliminary expectation from our models:
- If KV hit rate > 40% and average tokens/request remains ~1.6k, batching likely hits the $175/1M estimate.
- If KV hit rate < 20% or request length spikes, the streaming arm could be closer to $300/1M — we'll surface that risk in the sim.

Julie — I’ll include a simple PO-friendly summary in the Friday deliverable so procurement can approve quickly.

Schedule note: we can still kickoff Mar 7 if profiling results are green. If we see unexpected amplification we’ll flag and propose a short delay.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[ben@redwood.ai]
